authorship: AI review, authored by the DIS-RPLICE campaign loop (sprint 92, ledger item Q04). Not qualified human scientific acceptance, not clinical acceptance, and no patient benefit is claimed or implied.
change_from_0_1: period becomes a first-class field on every site object, so a per-site window cannot hide inside a single record-level string (S88-C4)

every one of the required dimensions must carry an explicit state and a reason on every record; absence is a validation failure, not a default (sprint 92 finding that 18 of 19 dimensions were absent yet the v0.1 validator returned PASS)
late_stage_share_percent must declare its construct, because the case proportion and the age-weighted rate ratio W coexist in the same record and differ by 0.7397 pp at Hinds and -0.5053 pp at Harris
claim_level is capped by comparison_status, so a CONDITIONAL comparison cannot carry a causal_candidate claim
follow_up_completion_after_abnormal_test is added as a required dimension, because the pilot's primary outcome was absent from v0.1 and neither system publishes it
share_rate_tolerance_basis: Not derivable from the published cells. Adopted by the DIS-RPLICE campaign loop as a materiality margin for a percentage-point share, because it exceeds both computable reconciliation floors computed in ledger item Q04 (0.1603448276 pp at Hinds and 0.2052631579 pp at Harris, S525-C2), and it is not a reconciliation tolerance. No accountable owner has ratified it. AI review, unverified by human: not qualified human scientific acceptance, not clinical acceptance, no patient benefit claimed.
share_rate_tolerance_representation_note: The share is the publisher's rounded one-decimal percentage. The values 375/589 and 5490/8660 are hypothetical count pairs compatible with rounded published displays, not identified registry totals. The November 8 denominator audit finds three compatible Hinds pairs and 25 Harris pairs. The 0.2723134290-percentage-point contrast and one-/two-case sensitivity based on one such pair are illustrative only. The published displayed contrast is 63.7 minus 63.4 = 0.3 percentage points; its unrounded value and uncertainty are not recovered. The 0.5-pp share/rate reconciliation margin is not a prespecified equivalence margin and cannot authorize an equivalence claim.

records.reason: Recorded 2019–2023 county estimates remain available for descriptive inspection. Both retained reports document regional-or-distant disease and a percentage relative to all-stage cases. Extract-specific stage derivation, alternate-variable exceptions, exact case-denominator exclusions and unrounded counts remain unresolved. Different pipeline labels alone do not establish a clinical classification mismatch. No harmonized comparison or statistical equivalence has been established.

denominator.why: For the case percentage, both retained interpretation pages say late-stage cases relative to all-stage cases, but do not disclose membership of unknown/unstaged, blank/unclassifiable, death-certificate-only or autopsy-only cases. Census population denominators apply to the incidence rates and cannot substitute for this case denominator.

age_adjustment.why: Rate footnotes specify 20 age groups for SEER and 19 for NPCR. Official February 2026 release history confirms that SEER incidence changed to 20 groups and NPCR did not. The CI*Rank note refers to 19 groups for both; column-level method linkage remains unresolved. This issue concerns incidence rates, not the crude case percentage; no harmonized county rate has been recalculated.

case_definition.why: Dagger footnote: rates are for invasive cancer only except bladder, computed from cancers classified as malignant on ICD-O-3, with cancer=020 the colorectal site set.

stage_definition.why: The displayed broad outcome is documented as regional or distant. The exact field, version, derivation and any alternate-variable exceptions remain undisclosed per extract. CDC NPCR SS2018 and NCI Derived SS2018 may support a common broad classification for 2019–2023; the expanded regional recode concerns pre-2018 cases and does not establish a mismatch here.

period.why: Report header states 2019-2023 for both county rows.

subgroup_coding.why: Table parameters fix the strata: race=00 All Races, sex=0 Both Sexes, age=001 All Ages.

suppression.why: Page states counts are suppressed below 16 records per area-sex-race category; the two county totals shown are far above that floor, but any age-stratified tabulation for Hinds does not clear it.

uncertainty.why: 95 percent confidence intervals printed beside each rate.

publication_latency.why: The page states a creation timestamp but not the registry data vintage or the release-to-publication interval for this window.

decision_owner.why: No named owner, reviewer or adjudicator is attached to this comparison in either repository or in the pilot register.

actionability.why: No action, threshold or owner is bound to this comparison; the sprint 78 counterfactual remains a proposal without an adopting body.

follow_up_completion_after_abnormal_test.why: Neither system publishes this quantity at county level, and the pilot's primary outcome has never been measured. When valued it must be: numerator, individuals with an abnormal screening-indication colorectal test who had a completed diagnostic colonoscopy with pathology documented within 180 days of the abnormal result; denominator, individuals with an abnormal screening-indication colorectal test in the same window; exclusions named in advance. A test ordered does not populate the numerator.
